steps.title: One pawn can be enough
steps.source: The gain of a Pawn is the smallest material advantage that can be obtained in a game; and it often is sufficient to win, even when the Pawn is the only remaining unit, apart from the Kings.

narration.say: A single extra pawn is the smallest advantage in chess. Yet it is often enough to win.
The rule: the king should be in front of its pawn, with at least one square in between.
But if the enemy king stands directly in front of the pawn, the game cannot be won.
In this lesson you defend with Black.

steps.title: Stay in front
steps.source: The way to proceed is for Black to keep the King always directly in front of the Pawn, and when it cannot be done […] then the Black King must be kept in front of the White King.

narration.say: Pawn to e3. The black king goes straight in front of it, to e5.
King to d3. Now Black cannot stay close to the pawn.
So the black king must stand in front of the white king instead. You are Black. Your move.

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Where must the black king go?

feedback.Ke6: Too far back. Capablanca: any other move but Kd5 loses.
feedback.Kf5: That is not in front of the white king. Now White's king goes ahead.
feedback.Kf6: Too far back. Bring the king as far forward as possible.
feedback.Kd6: Too far back. Bring the king as far forward as possible, in front of the white king.
feedback.*: Stand as far forward as possible, and directly in front of the white king.

exercise.hint: The white king is on d3. Stand in front of it.
exercise.success: Yes: 2... Kd5. A very important move. Any other move would lose. White pushes the pawn with check.

steps.title: The dance of the kings
steps.source: As the White King comes up, the Black King must be kept in front of it, since it cannot be brought up to the Pawn.

narration.say: Black returns in front of the pawn, to e5.
King to e3. Black to e6.
King to f4. Black to f6, again in front of the white king.
Pawn to e5, check. Black to e6.
King to e4. Black to e7.
King to d5. Black to d7.
Pawn to e6, check. Black to e7.
King to e5. Black to e8.
King to d6. Your move again.

exercise.prompt: Black to move. Keep the draw.

feedback.Kf8: After Kf8, White plays Kd7 and the pawn runs to e8. Stand in front of the white king.
feedback.*: Stand directly in front of the white king.

exercise.hint: The white king is on d6.
exercise.success: Correct: 11... Kd8. Black is in front of the white king. The draw is safe.

steps.title: Why it is a draw
steps.source: If now White advances the Pawn, the Black King gets in front of it and White must either give up the Pawn or play K - K 6, and a stale mate results.

narration.say: If White pushes the pawn to e7, check, the black king steps in front of it.
Now White must either give up the pawn, or play king to e6.
King to e6: Black has no legal move, but is not in check. Stalemate. A draw.

steps.title: What we learned
steps.source: The whole mode of procedure is very important and the student should become thoroughly conversant with its details.

narration.say: The defender keeps his king directly in front of the pawn.
When that is not possible, he keeps it in front of the enemy king, as far forward as possible.
Capablanca could not stress it enough: many beginners have lost identical positions.
